title: Compact hub carousel navigation prototype for contextual dashboards and quick workspace actions
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The current console navigation mixes global routes, workspace switching, and per-route controls in a long left rail which pushes critical dashboard and rollout controls below the fold. Users with multiple workspaces and frequent context switches lose time hunting for cost views, rollout toggles, and recent dashboards.

Goal: Validate a compact, horizontally-scrollable 'hub carousel' that surfaces 1) top-priority dashboards, 2) active rollouts & quick toggle actions, and 3) workspace chips for fast context switch. The pattern should preserve discoverability for deep routes while reducing vertical clutter on smaller viewports.

Scope: Low-fidelity -> high-fidelity prototypes for desktop and tablet, heuristic review with PM/Eng, interactive Figma flows for: 
- Dashboard-first mode (carousel prioritizes dashboards and metrics)
- Route-first mode (carousel pins routes and recent queries)
- Workspace quick-actions (contextual chips with keyboard hotkeys)

Success metrics (validate in usability sessions and pilot): 
- Average time-to-switch-workspace <= 3s for power users
- 20% reduction in vertical scroll to access cost/rollout controls on 1440px screens
- No increase in error rate when launching rollouts from carousel

Trade-offs considered: 
- Hiding full route tree in a secondary panel reduces information scent vs. persistent left rail. Decided to retain an optional compact rail for users who prefer full nav.
- Horizontal carousel increases discoverability of top items but may hide low-frequency routes; addressed via quick-search and persistent overflow menu.

Deliverables: 
- Figma prototypes (desktop/tablet) with annotated interaction specs
- Research script and 8 moderated usability sessions
- Implementation handoff package with component specs and accessibility checklist

Next steps: 
- Complete high-fidelity prototype and motion spec (by 2025-11-25) 
- Run 6 usability sessions (target: 2025-12-05) 
- Sync with Eng on interaction budget and keyboard shortcuts (sync on 2025-11-18)

2025-11-18 - Devon Brooks (Eng): Concern about rendering cost of a horizontally scrolling list with many dynamic items. Suggest we implement virtualization and limit carousel to 12 visible items with overflow handling. We'll prototype an efficient list in the runtime demo. Action: ENG to sketch perf constraints by 2025-11-22.

2025-11-20 - Rana Iqbal (Design Review): Heuristic feedback - contrast for chip states is low at 75% zoom. Increase focus ring and ensure keyboard-only users can cycle through chips. Add aria-describedby for rollout toggles.

2025-11-22 - Claire Nguyen (Designer): Iteration 2 uploaded to Figma with motion frames, keyboard nav, and overflow menu patterns. Link posted below. Added variant for pinned-rail users where the carousel collapses to a compact chevron tray.

2025-11-26 - Marco Santos (PM): Quick research brief approved. Please prioritize sessions with mid-market customers (platform teams) who manage multiple workspaces. Also include an A/B pilot plan with Dedicated customers.

2025-11-29 - Devon Brooks (Eng): Reviewed hi-fi and motion spec. Implementation risk: focus trap when opening quick-action popovers. We'll prototype with the accessibility team and add e2e test coverage. Estimated front-end work: 5 dev days.
